title: Martin Payne, James Linton, Kirk Lyons, and Robert Woodward v. Western Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC answered both stated issues “No,” denying the consolidated complaints: Presbytery did not err either in conducting the BCO 31-2 investigation or in finding no strong presumption of guilt. Lyons and Woodward additionally lacked standing because they were not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction. No further investigation, process, or other relief was ordered.
first_summary: Four complainants challenged Presbytery’s investigation of accusations against a minister and its finding that no strong presumption of guilt existed. The SJC denied the complaints, holding that BCO 31-2 grants investigating courts great procedural discretion and does not require interviews or a particular timetable. Finding no clear constitutional error, it deferred to Presbytery’s superior familiarity with the facts and parties.
summary: Four complainants challenged Presbytery’s BCO 31-2 investigation and its finding of no strong presumption of guilt, citing delayed action and failure to interview accusers. The SJC denied the complaints: BCO 31-2 requires due diligence but grants great discretion and prescribes neither interviews nor a timetable, and the record showed no clear constitutional error overcoming deference to Presbytery. Lyons and Woodward also lacked standing because they were not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction. No renewed investigation or process was ordered.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The consolidated caption and SJC disposition appear at lines 1–3 and 11; the panel decision was amended by the full SJC, with 21 concurring, at lines 274–278.
evidence_notes.dispute: The stated issues challenge the investigation’s conduct and Presbytery’s no-strong-presumption finding (lines 195–205); the asserted defects were omitted interviews and delay (lines 207–214).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Both issues were answered “No” (lines 201–205). BCO 31-2 prescribes no interviews or timetable, and no clear error displaced lower-court deference (lines 211–227, 266–272).
evidence_notes.qualifications: Lyons and Woodward lacked standing because they were not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction (lines 261–264). The investigation phase was distinguished from instituted process (lines 231–245).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No separate decision was incorporated by reference. The record notes that the investigating committee’s Attachment G was absent, but states its finding and Presbytery’s acceptance (lines 121–123).
